insulin age reference crosses zero and is labelled inconclusive

nhanes_insulin: BMI direction is positive in all six draws; both constructions underestimate the weighted coefficient: generated medians 0.2379 and 0.2517 versus reference 0.2959 per five BMI units. This is partial conditional-analysis transport, not accurate magnitude recovery.

Quadratic curvature is negative in all six draws, agreeing with the negative reference. Magnitude is attenuated, especially ia: medians -0.02065 and -0.03909 versus -0.05175. The endpoint was assumption-dependent before generation; this result does not identify a biological curve or validate the assumed functional form.

Female-minus-male BMI slope is near zero in both constructions and changes sign across residual draws, while reference is -0.1193 with descriptive 95% CI [-0.1710,-0.06762]. Neither construction recovers this interaction magnitude; two agreeing signs in three draws must not be presented as successful interaction recovery.

The adjusted age reference is -0.01171 with 95% CI [-0.02551,0.00209], crossing zero. ia has three negative signs; ib has one negative and two positive. This is a point-direction difference with an inconclusive reference zero-null screen, not a demonstrated biological-direction failure or absent-effect result.
pns_hba1c: Age direction is positive in all six weighted and all six unweighted draws. Weighted medians 0.1589 and 0.1563 are above the reference 0.1470 percentage points per decade; this is source-relation transport, not discovery of an age relationship.

BMI direction is positive throughout but both constructions underestimate magnitude: weighted medians 0.09061 and 0.10434 versus 0.16104 percentage points per five BMI units. The attenuation persists unweighted.

Reference curvature is positive under both provided weights (0.04089) and unweighted sensitivity (0.01680). ha is negative in every draw under both analyses; hb is negative in one draw and positive in two, with smaller positive medians. Thus ha fails point-direction reproduction and hb is unstable. Missing survey design precludes a reference uncertainty-based conclusion.

The interaction is positive in both reference point analyses but residual-draw signs fluctuate in both constructions; ha has only one matching unweighted sign. A median near the reference, especially hb, does not establish stable interaction recovery. No PNS design-based CIs are available.
interpretation.overall: Executable enrichment and reuse of the same fixed analyses are demonstrated, with mixed fidelity. Stable transported age/BMI directions coexist with systematic magnitude attenuation and failures or instability in assumption-dependent curvature/interaction. No aggregate success threshold, method-superiority comparison, clinical-effect conclusion or equivalence claim is justified.
interpretation.secondary_reuse: All 18 age-sex-BMI cell means, secondary sex coefficients and diagnostics are retained; PNS repeats the entire family unweighted. NHANES HOMA1 is derived use, not independent confirmation.

limitations: Only two tasks and two independently built constructions per task; residual seeds and correlated endpoints are not independent tasks.
Residual ranges quantify only Monte Carlo variation, not source, model, transport, reference or clinical uncertainty.
NHANES intervals are descriptive, unadjusted, design-based association intervals with prespecified conservative residual degrees of freedom; no clinical importance margin or causal interpretation.
PNS supplies weights but no PSU/strata; national calibration remains unresolved and baseline covariates precede laboratory outcomes.
Age and related BMI associations were already in source evidence. Curvature and sex-slope interaction were classified assumption-dependent; structural sensitivity was not established.
Source replays use approximated joint covariates and cross-study fusion is incomplete. Procedural builder custody is not OS-level agent isolation.
